NEW DELHI: Indian para-swimmer Himanshu Nandal made his mark at the Asian Para Games 2026 in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, completing a hat-trick of bronze medals with another podium finish in the men's 100m freestyle S11 event on Friday.The 22-year-old clocked 1 minute 5.90 seconds to finish third, behind Japan's Uchu Tomita, who won gold in a Games-record time of 58.22 seconds, and China's Chuanzhen Sun, who took silver in 58.70 seconds.Nandal's latest medal added to his earlier bronze finishes in the men's 400m freestyle and 100m breaststroke S11 events. He became one of India's standout performers in para swimming, matching compatriot Ravi Budigina's three-medal haul at the Games, which comprised two silver medals and a bronze.Born blind due to optic nerve failure, Nandal grew up in a sports-oriented family in Rohtak, Haryana. His father had played hockey at the national level, and sport became part of his life from an early age.At four, Nandal moved to Delhi and joined the National Association for the Blind, where he learnt Braille. He initially took up judo and went on to win medals at the national level before switching to swimming in 2021.The change opened a new chapter in his sporting journey, as he quickly progressed from domestic competitions to the international stage.Nandal achieved a significant milestone in 2024 when he became the first Indian blind swimmer to meet the Minimum Qualification Standard for the Paris Paralympics.A political science graduate from the University of Delhi's Atma Ram Sanatan Dharma College, he continued to build his experience against international opposition. In 2025, he reached two finals at the World Para Swimming Championships in Singapore.At the Asian Para Games, Nandal began his medal-winning run on Tuesday, clocking 5:10.91 to secure bronze in the men's 400m freestyle S11 event. He followed it up with another third-place finish in the 100m breaststroke before completing his hat-trick in the 100m freestyle on Friday.The S11 classification is for swimmers with visual impairment, including those with very low visual acuity or no light perception.Nandal's three-medal campaign in Japan marks another milestone in his progress as an Indian para-swimmer and adds to his growing experience at major international competitions.
Article Summary: Himanshu Nandal completes hat-trick of bronze medals at Asian Para Games 2026. The 22-year-old finished third in the men's 100m freestyle S11 event on Friday. Nandal is the first Indian blind swimmer to meet the Minimum Qualification Standard for the Paris Paralympics.

The Indian pair wrapped up the contest in just 28 minutes.Thulasimathi had earlier settled for silver in the women's singles SU5 final, losing 18-21, 11-21 to China's Yang. Paris Paralympic silver medallist defeats China's Yang Qiuxia and Xiao Zuxian 21-16, 21-13 in women's doubles final. Article Title: Why Cristiano Ronaldo, 41, refuses to drink milk: Inside the diet and discipline behind his longevity, according to former chef
Article Text:
Cristiano Ronaldo's former chef reveals why the 41-year-old superstar refuses milk as part of his strict diet and fitness routine.

Why Ronaldo refuses to drink milk

What Ronaldo eats throughout the day

Ronaldo maintains under 10% body fat, avoids refined sugar, milk, and focuses on strict recovery routines/ Instagram

The training and recovery behind his longevity

Ronaldo’s recovery routine includes intense sauna sessions and ice baths to maintain peak fitness and longevity/Instagram

Why Ronaldo's former chef agrees with Haaland about organ meat

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

At 41, Cristiano Ronaldo is still chasing a milestone that once seemed beyond the reach of any footballer, with his career tally approaching 1,000 goals after another prolific season for Al-Nassr. His longevity has been built on an unusually disciplined approach to training, recovery and nutrition, although one of the strictest rules in his diet concerns a food that many athletes regard as an everyday source of protein and calcium. According to his former private chef, Giorgio Barone, Ronaldo does not drink milk at all.Milk is commonly included in athletes’ diets because of its protein, calcium and other nutrients, with many players using it as part of their recovery routine. Ronaldo, however, has avoided dairy as part of his long-standing nutritional approach, a decision his former private chef says reflects more than a preference about taste or performance.Giorgio Barone, who previously worked as Ronaldo’s private chef, explained that milk was completely excluded from the forward’s diet because of his views on humans consuming the milk of other animals.“No milk,” Barone told Covers.com, before explaining his reasoning.“Humans are the only animals that drink the milk of other animals. No other animal drinks milk after three months. Calves don’t drink milk after the age of three months. Animals don’t drink the milk of other animals.“It does not exist in nature. Only human beings continue to drink milk up to 30, 40, 50, and 60 years, and in my view it is wrong. We breastfeed from our mothers, like dogs, wolves, cows and donkeys. It is normal.“After infancy it is not normal. It is against nature.”Barone's explanation is his own view of nutrition, rather than an established medical consensus, but it illustrates how deliberately Ronaldo has approached the food he consumes throughout his career. Dairy is not the only category he avoids, with the Portuguese forward also known for steering clear of refined sugar, processed foods and alcohol.Barone described Ronaldo's diet as balanced rather than built around a single food group, with the emphasis placed on fresh ingredients, lean protein and vegetables. The former chef said the forward eats a little of everything, provided it meets the standards of his nutritional routine.“Cristiano Ronaldo’s diet is balanced,” he said. “He eats a little bit of everything, but it’s always healthy.”Breakfast typically includes avocado, coffee and eggs, with no added sugar. Lunch can consist of chicken or fish accompanied by vegetables, while dinner is generally lighter, with fish or meat served alongside vegetables.“Starting with breakfast, he would have an avocado with coffee, eggs and no sugar. Absolutely no sugar. Lunch could be chicken, fish and always vegetables. If he needs carbohydrates, he gets them through vegetables, so he doesn’t need anything made with flour.“Nothing like pasta, bread and other types of food. In the evening, he eats light foods, usually fish or meat in the form of fillet. It’s always accompanied by vegetables.”The broader nutritional approach described in the additional account of Ronaldo's routine includes as many as six high-protein meals a day, spaced three to four hours apart. Chicken, cod, sea bass, fresh vegetables and avocado feature prominently, while quinoa and other whole grains provide carbohydrate sources alongside the vegetables mentioned by Barone. The emphasis remains on whole foods and consistent meals rather than relying on processed products or sugary snacks.That routine is designed to support the physical demands of a player who continues to compete at the highest level well into his forties. Ronaldo's body fat has been reported at below 10 per cent, with some accounts putting it at around seven per cent, although the exact figure can vary with the timing and method of measurement.Ronaldo's approach extends well beyond what he eats.
